### Hover card
Shows a card of preview content after a delay when a link is hovered or gets keyboard focus.

Component ID: `hover-card`

[Component documentation](https://www.expressivecss.com/hover-card.html.md) · [Repository source](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/blob/master/docs/src/pages/hover-card.astro) · [Matching tag](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/tree/v0.15.0)

Contract: ExpressiveCSS 0.15.0

Contract SHA-256: `c240c761f0874a1923c3701691601ed8defc928c4f35d1fb7ed812a17955abad`

#### Selection and adaptation

Runtime ownership: `auto-init`. No dedicated entry in the reviewed Google component inventory.

Example: An author name in an article previews the author's profile in a hover card; an icon button's label is a tooltip, and a note people open on press is a popover.

#### Material mapping

Relationship: none. Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

Upstream: web-extension-inventory-reviewed (2026-10-25); [evidence](https://m3.material.io/components).

Requirements and boundaries: design reference web-extensions-review. The inventory page renders client-side, so this review relies on the 2026-09-13 inventory review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.

Support (2026-10-25, `llm.md#hover-card`): A link with hover-card-trigger whose aria-details names a .popover with popover="hint"; the card shows against the link after enterDelay of hover or keyboard focus, stays while the pointer or focus is on the link or card, hides after exitDelay or at once on Escape with focus back on the link, and a tap or click follows the link.

Web adaptation: Script timers decide when the card shows, and showPopover({ source }) makes the link its anchor and invoker, so the browser places it, puts it next in the Tab order and light-dismisses it. Interest invokers (interestfor) exist only in Chromium, so they are not used.

Known boundary: Hover delay, a pointer that passes over, staying open on the card, hiding after exitDelay, keyboard focus, Tab into the card, Escape with focus back on the link, focus leaving the card and a click that focuses the link are checked in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit; spoken output and aria-details support in screen readers remain unverified. Touch shows no card, and the card's content is static markup.

Full parity remains unassessed. [Capability evidence](../references/capability-roadmap.md#hover-card).

#### Contract

Add `hover-card-trigger` to an `<a href>` and point its `aria-details` at the card, a `.popover` with `popover="hint"`. `AutoInit()` starts every `.hover-card-trigger`. Once the pointer or keyboard focus has rested on the link for `enterDelay`, 500 ms by default, the card shows against the link: below it with start edges aligned, flipped to the other side when it would not fit. A pointer that only passes over the link shows nothing.

The card stays while the pointer is on the link or the card, and while focus is on either. When both are left, it hides after `exitDelay`, 300 ms by default, so a pointer that crosses the gap to the card keeps it open. Focus stays on the link when the card shows, and Tab moves into the card's links and buttons. Escape hides the card and takes focus in it back to the link. A click elsewhere hides it too. One hint card shows at a time, and a hover card leaves an open menu or popover alone. Several links can name the same card, such as a name mentioned twice, and the card shows against whichever link showed it last.

A tap or click follows the link and shows no card, so the linked page has to hold the same content for touch screens. Keep the card a short preview of where the link goes, and put anything to act on in the page, a popover opened by a button or a dialog. Do not also give the link `interestfor`, which Chromium would handle on its own as well.

#### Syntax

```html
<p>Written by <a class="hover-card-trigger" href="/people/ada" aria-details="ada-card">Ada Lovelace</a>.</p>
<div id="ada-card" class="popover" popover="hint">
  <h3>Ada Lovelace</h3>
  <p>Mathematician. Wrote the first published program, for the Analytical Engine.</p>
  <p><a href="/people/ada/articles">All articles by Ada</a></p>
</div>
```

#### Options

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enterDelay` | Number | `500` | How long the pointer or keyboard focus rests on the link before the card shows, in milliseconds. |
| `exitDelay` | Number | `300` | How long the card stays after the pointer and focus leave the link and the card, in milliseconds. |

#### Methods

- `.open()`: Shows the card now, without `enterDelay`.
- `.close()`: Hides the card now, without `exitDelay`.
- `.destroy()`: Hides a card the instance showed and removes the listeners. The link and card keep the markup as written.

#### Also documented

The Hover card section of the [API reference](https://www.expressivecss.com/llm.md) also covers Accessibility, Events.

#### Rules

- `hover-card-trigger-is-a-link`: Put hover-card-trigger on an <a href>. The card previews where the link goes, and a tap or click still has to follow it; a button already has a popover that opens on press.
- `hover-card-names-its-card`: Point the trigger's aria-details at the id of its card, a [popover] element in the page. The component finds the card through it, and screen readers use it to reach the card.
